itCapacity.note: Chosen for this model: about 45% more than the largest datacenter estimated to be running today.

largestRunning.note: Anthropic–Amazon New Carlisle (Indiana), IT power estimated by Epoch AI from satellite images and permits; not confirmed by the operator. xAI Colossus 2 is close (≈946 MW).

largestPlanned.note: Meta Hyperion, Louisiana, eventual capacity announced by Mark Zuckerberg. Epoch AI projects about 1,632 MW by 2028.

pue.note: Lowest campus PUE in Google's published table: Central Ohio (Lancaster). A small research HPC site (NREL ESIF) reports 1.036.

pueResearch.note: Range reported across immersion-cooling studies; cooling part only.

energyYear.note: At full load all year: an upper bound. Real sites run below their capacity (FRA21 averaged about a third).

coolant.note: NVIDIA Vera Rubin: liquid at 45 °C straight to the chips; NVIDIA says no chillers are needed. Cooling makers say some sites will still need them.

hotDays.note: Days a year reaching 30 °C at Luleå-Kallax.

wueProven.note: Meta's fleet average: the lowest fleet WUE we found.

waterProvenM3.formula: IT energy at full load × 0.20 L/kWh

zeroWater.note: Microsoft's closed-loop design, announced August 2024; first sites in Phoenix and Mt Pleasant from 2026, online late 2027. Microsoft: avoids more than 125 million litres a year per datacenter, at a slightly higher PUE.

zeroWaterProven.value: closed warm-water loop with dry coolers
zeroWaterProven.note: Already done at small scale: NREL's ESIF supercomputer centre.

heatYear.formula: IT energy at full load (almost all of it ends up as heat)

luleaHeat.note: District heat delivered by LuleKraft to Luleå Energi; the most recent public figure. About 31,000 households are connected (SVT, 2026).

luleaGas.value: the town's main heat source, gas from the SSAB blast furnace, is due to shut in 2030

heatTimesLulea.formula: heat a year ÷ Luleå's district heat

erfMax.note: Even if the campus heated all of Luleå all year (it cannot in summer), it would reuse only this share of its energy. Germany's law asks new sites for 20% from 2028.

odense.value: ≈ 45 MW of heat, 215,000 MWh recovered, more than 12,000 homes (2023)
odense.note: Meta Odense, Denmark: heat pumps lift server heat to 70–75 °C for the town network.

espoo.value: about 40% of the district heat of Espoo, Kauniainen and Kirkkonummi (≈ 2 TWh a year)
espoo.note: Fortum and Microsoft; heat plants started May 2026, heat from the datacenters from 2027.

gridCO2.note: Sweden, counting imports and exports. No figure for Luleå's own bidding zone (SE1) was found.

cfeStockholm.note: Google's Stockholm cloud region: carbon-free electricity hour by hour (rounded).

nuclearPromise.value: Google–Kairos: 500 MW of small reactors by 2035, first 50 MW unit from 2030; Amazon–X-energy: up to 5 GW by 2039
nuclearPromise.note: No small modular reactor powers a datacenter today.

battery.note: Replaced diesel generators at a Microsoft datacenter in Sweden (site not named).

batteryScaled.note: What the same 80 minutes would take at this size.

hydrogen.value: 3 MW hydrogen fuel cell passed Microsoft's generator tests

timber.value: about 95% of the frame in cross-laminated timber; operator claims up to 60% lower embodied carbon

timberMs.value: 35% less embodied carbon than steel, 65% less than precast concrete (estimated)
timberMs.note: Microsoft, two hybrid-timber datacenters in Northern Virginia.

chips.value: up to 50× more AI output per watt than the previous generation
chips.note: NVIDIA GB300 vs Hopper, for specific models and settings; later tests show up to 25×.

noiseMeasured.note: Loudoun County: readings at the home next to a Vantage campus never went above this.

noiseNight.note: Night limit at the nearest home that a sound study says low-noise coolers and sound walls can meet.

flex.note: Emerald AI cut an Oracle datacenter's AI power by 25% for 3 hours during a grid peak in Phoenix (256 GPUs).

flexDeals.value: Google agreed to cut machine-learning power on request of two US utilities

neighbour.value: Meta Luleå, running since 2013; no public heat-export deal found
